statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Every published hour falls inside the scheduled weekend halt of CME equity-index futures and the NAS100 CFD, so no pathological Nasdaq-100 price path can form inside the window, while the macro backdrop behind elevated Stress remains unresolved.
recommendation: Tail stays far below the block threshold across the full published window because no tradable Nasdaq-100 venue exists until Sunday 22:00Z. Elevated Stress reflects the unchanged long-end yield and energy backdrop rather than any observed mean-reversion failure, and reopen gap risk falls outside this window.
headline: Nasdaq-100 inside the scheduled CME weekend closure after an orderly Friday advance; Tail at its floor with Stress elevated on 5.18% long-end yields and $92 crude
body: Friday's session finished in orderly two-sided fashion. Cash NDX closed 30,608.14, up 0.42%, inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 range and roughly 0.2% below the day's high, while NQ Dec-26 settled 30,919.00, up 0.49%. VIX fell 5.11% to 14.87 and all three major US averages posted weekly gains, with the Dow snapping a three-week losing streak. Retracements occurred repeatedly through the session and the index did not pin to an extreme, so no evidence of persistent one-way structure or repeated extension after failed pullbacks is present. CME equity-index futures settled at 21:00Z and do not reopen until Sunday 22:00Z, which is beyond the final published hour; the NAS100 CFD follows the same closure. Because sustained mean-reversion failure requires a tradable price path, Tail is held at its floor for every hour of the window. The environment behind Stress is nonetheless genuinely difficult and unresolved: the 10-year Treasury yield is 5.18% and the 30-year sits near 5.5%, around its highest since 2004, after touching multi-decade highs earlier in the week; WTI is $92.44, down 2.29% on Friday on renewed discussion of a return to the lapsed US-Iran interim deal but still roughly 12% higher over the month, with the Strait of Hormuz effectively closed since 28 February 2026 and about a fifth of seaborne oil trade disrupted. Attacks on commercial shipping have continued, including damage to the tanker LR Stephanie on 22 September, and no September diplomatic breakthrough has been verified. Final Michigan sentiment printed 48.1 with one-year inflation expectations at 4.6%. Shared Finviz context was fresh at collection but partial, with its futures and calendar sections unavailable; its delayed latest-session breadth showed Technology up 0.85% and semiconductors up 0.56%, used only as confirmation alongside independently verified levels. Stress is therefore held in the elevated band throughout, easing modestly through the quiet weekend hours and firming back toward the end of the window as unpriced headline flow accumulates ahead of the reopen. Confidence starts at 86 on a complete set of verified closing levels, yields, energy prices, volatility and calendar detail, and decays across the window purely as Friday's last verified observation ages.

lookbackSummary: Across the trailing 24 hours the published Claude state ranged between Tail 10 and 22 and never approached the block threshold. The overnight and early European stretch held Tail at 17-20 in normal conditions, three trend-up prints appeared between 06:00Z and 11:00Z as the index worked higher, and the US cash session settled back into mixed conditions at Tail 18-19. The final two published hours dropped to Tail 12 and then 10 as CME futures settled into the weekend closure and no tradable price path remained. Stress stayed in the elevated band between 49 and 59 throughout, reflecting the long-end yield and energy backdrop rather than any observed mean-reversion failure, and Confidence held between 86 and 88. One hour, 13:00Z, has no published assessment and is marked unavailable rather than reconstructed.
outlookSummary: The entire published window falls inside the scheduled CME weekend closure: futures settled at 21:00Z on Friday and do not reopen until Sunday 22:00Z, past the final slot. Tail is held between 9 and 11 for all 24 hours because sustained mean-reversion failure requires a tradable price path, and none of the inherited amplifiers can be observed while every Nasdaq-100 venue is shut. Stress eases from 48 toward 45 through the quiet overnight and Saturday morning hours and firms back to 50 into the end of the window as unpriced weekend headline flow accumulates ahead of the reopen; the unresolved Strait of Hormuz closure, continuing attacks on shipping and the 5.18% 10-year yield keep it inside the elevated band throughout. Confidence decays from 86 to 74 purely as Friday's last verified observation ages across the weekend gap. No evidence-based danger window is published, because a pathological price path cannot form inside a closed market; the first genuine tests of the tape are next week's scheduled checkpoints, led by August core PCE on Wednesday and September payrolls on Friday, all of which sit beyond this window.
